fair_value.method: Forward P/E: by Sept 2027 the market prices FY2028 EPS; consensus FY2027 EPS $9.58 (range $8.69-$10.67) grown ~10% as memory costs ease in 2028 gives FY2028 EPS ~$10.50. Applying 32x (below today's ~35.6x forward multiple, above Apple's ~25-30x 5-year average, justified by high-single-digit EPS growth, ~$100B/yr buybacks and a strong iPhone cycle) gives ~$335.

bear.story: Memory inflation (the '100-year flood') plus the lower-than-hoped Duo pricing push gross margin toward 45-46%, Services slows to high single digits (App Store softness, Epic/SCOTUS, a DOJ appeal that threatens the ~$20B Google default-search payment), and supply limits cap the iPhone 18/Duo cycle. FY2027 EPS about $9.2 and the multiple de-rates to about 26-27x, giving ~$250.

base.story: The iPhone 18 Pro/Duo cycle delivers high-single-digit to low-double-digit revenue growth in FY2027 and EPS close to consensus ($9.6-10.0). Gross margin dips about 100bp and then recovers as memory eases into 2028. The multiple compresses slightly to ~33x on FY2028 EPS of ~$10.5-10.6, so the stock goes roughly sideways from here to modestly higher.

bull.story: A genuine super-cycle: the Duo sells everything Apple can build, the Siri AI relaunch drives upgrades and Services re-accelerates, and memory normalizes faster. FY2028 EPS reaches ~$11.5 and the market keeps paying a ~38x 'AI hardware platform' multiple, giving ~$440 (in line with the most bullish sell-side targets of ~$400-405 plus a year of drift).

thesis_break_reason: About 25% below the current price and close to the 52-week low ($243). At ~$255 the stock would trade at about 26-27x consensus FY2027 EPS, a de-rating that ordinary 25% volatility is unlikely to produce by itself. It would most likely mean earnings were cut: gross margin falling well below 46% on memory costs, the iPhone 18/Duo cycle disappointing, or a legal/regulatory hit to Services such as losing the Google search payment or an adverse App Store ruling.

key_uncertainties: How long and how deep the DRAM/NAND cost inflation lasts, and how much margin Apple gives up to protect volume
Supply constraints on advanced nodes and memory capping iPhone, Mac and Duo shipments
Whether the Services slowdown (12% in FQ3, ~9.5% guided) is FX/App Store noise or structural, especially given the Google payment and App Store legal risk
Whether a ~35x forward multiple on a ~10% EPS grower is sustainable; the multiple is the biggest swing factor
Execution under the new CEO, John Ternus, and whether Siri AI is competitive
Macro, tariffs, and a broad tech/AI de-rating
reasoning: Facts: the stock closed at $341.07, a record area after the iPhone 18 Pro/Duo and Siri AI launches and the start of John Ternus's tenure as CEO on Sept 1. FQ3 2026 revenue was $109.4B (+16%) and EPS $2.02 (+29%, including $0.11 of tariff refunds). Guidance for FQ4 is revenue +9-11% and gross margin 47-48%, down from 50.1% on memory costs and supply constraints. Consensus EPS is FY2026 $8.82 and FY2027 $9.58, so the stock trades at ~35.6x forward earnings, historically rich for ~9-10% EPS growth. Sell-side targets average ~$328 (median $340, range $215-405), roughly at the current price, and Morningstar calls the stock 'lightly expensive' ($290). My fair value is ~$335: FY2028 EPS of ~$10.5 at 32x. That is slightly below spot, but a strong product cycle and heavy buybacks offset it, so the base case is roughly flat to modestly up. The scenario mix (25% at $250, 50% at $350, 25% at $440) has a mean of ~$348. For the ladder I used a lognormal centered near $345 with ~27% log-volatility (the 25% realized vol plus a little extra for the multiple and legal risk). I then fattened the left tail slightly because of the rich valuation and margin and legal risk, and trimmed the far right tail because a sustained 40x+ multiple is unlikely. The result is P(>=341) ≈ 0.51, a ~21% chance the stock is below $273 and a ~13% chance it is above $460. I did not use option-implied data.
